outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to LLMs in Tabular Learning
outline.description: This chapter introduces the intersection of Large Language Models (LLMs) and tabular data analysis. It defines the challenges of few-shot learning in tabular domains, reviews existing approaches that treat LLMs as end-to-end predictors, and motivates the paradigm shift toward using LLMs as automated feature engineers.
subtopics: The rise of Large Language Models and their reasoning capabilities
Challenges in few-shot tabular learning: Spurious correlations and data scarcity
Limitations of current LLM-based tabular methods: Cost, latency, and context window constraints
The FeatLLM hypothesis: Leveraging LLMs for rule extraction rather than direct prediction
Overview of the FeatLLM framework and its key contributions

outline.description: This chapter provides the theoretical background necessary to understand FeatLLM. It covers traditional few-shot learning techniques for tabular data, the evolution of language-interfaced tabular learning, and the specific gaps in literature that FeatLLM addresses.
subtopics: Traditional few-shot learning strategies: Semi-supervised learning and data augmentation
Transfer learning in tabular domains: Pre-training on diverse datasets
Language-Interfaced Tabular Learning: Serializing data and prompting strategies
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning vs. In-context learning
Critical analysis of baselines: TabLLM, STUNT, and TabPFN

outline.description: A deep dive into the structural design of FeatLLM. This chapter breaks down the workflow from raw tabular data to final class likelihood estimation, emphasizing the separation between the feature generation phase (LLM-driven) and the inference phase (lightweight ML model).
subtopics: Problem formulation: Definitions of datasets, features, and k-shot settings
High-level architecture overview: The two-stage pipeline
Stage 1: Rule Extraction via In-Context Learning
Stage 2: Feature Transformation and Binary Encoding
Stage 3: Downstream Classification with Linear Models
Advantages of decoupling feature engineering from inference

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Prompt Engineering for Rule Discovery
outline.description: This chapter details the specific prompt design strategies used to coax high-quality logical rules from LLMs. It explains how to structure prompts to mimic expert human reasoning, ensuring the extraction of causal relationships rather than spurious correlations.
subtopics: Component 1: Basic Information Description (Task, Features, Examples)
Data serialization formats for tabular inputs
Component 2: Reasoning Instructions (Chain-of-Thought adaptation)
Step-by-step reasoning: Inferring causal tendencies before rule derivation
Component 3: Response Formatting Constraints
Handling feature types and preventing logical inconsistencies in generated rules

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 5: From Natural Language Rules to Executable Features
outline.description: This chapter addresses the technical challenge of converting unstructured natural language rules into executable code for feature generation. It explores using LLMs as parsers to handle syntactic variability and discusses the mathematical formulation for estimating class likelihood.
subtopics: The parsing challenge: Syntactic noise in LLM outputs
"LLM-as-a-Parser": Generating Python code from natural language rules
Executing generated code safely to create binary feature vectors
Mathematical formulation of class likelihood estimation
Learning feature importance via constrained linear weights (Non-negative projection)
Optimization objectives: Cross-entropy loss in low-data regimes

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 6: Robustness through Ensembling and Bagging
outline.description: This chapter explains how FeatLLM overcomes LLM stochasticity and context window limitations. It details the implementation of bagging strategies for both samples and features, and how ensembling multiple weak learners leads to a robust final predictor.
subtopics: The role of temperature and demonstration ordering in rule diversity
Feature Bagging: Managing high-dimensional data within context limits
Sample Bagging: Enhancing stability in few-shot scenarios
The Ensemble Mechanism: Aggregating probabilities across multiple trials
Miti gating single-point failures and incorrect rule generation via self-consistency

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 7: Experimental Evaluation and Results Analysis
outline.description: This chapter presents a comprehensive review of the empirical results reported in the paper. It compares FeatLLM against nine distinct baselines across thirteen diverse datasets, analyzing performance metrics, computational costs, and scalability.
subtopics: Dataset diversity:Benchmarking on real-world,synthetic,and temporal-shifted data
Performance comparison:AUC metrics against LogReg,XGBoost,and LLM-baselines
The efficiency gap:Few-shot performance(4 shots)vs.traditional methods(32 shots)
Computational cost analysis：Training time，API queries，and inference latency
Scalability testing：Performance on datasets with hundreds of features

outline.description: This chapter dissects the internal mechanics of FeatLLM through rigorous ablation studies.It evaluates the contribution of each architectural component,prompt element,and hyperparameter to isolate sourcesof performance gain.
subtopics: Impactof weight tuning vs.simple counting mechanisms
The necessityofensemblemethodsforrobustness
Valueoffeaturedescriptionsandreasoninginstructionsinfew-shotsettings
Hyperparameter sensitivity:Numberofensemblesandrulesperclass
Feature quality assessment：AUROCofgeneratedrulesbeforeandaftertuning
Robustnessagainstspuriouscorrelations:noisyfeatureinjectionexperiments
